# Status/issuance Badge

Figma: [04b. Status/issuance Badge](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-912) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-01

Two-layer badge family. Layer 1 is the generic Badge primitive (Dot for presence, Count for numeric overflow). Layer 2 is the IssuanceStatusBadge - three audience-specific sets (Investor, Developer, Internal) that map Safqah's 25-status issuance lifecycle to user-facing pill badges with copy and color tied to the spec at "Issuance Status Copy - Safqah Capital." Strictly: badge visibility, label text, and palette are derived from the markdown source of truth; deviations should be propagated back to the spec, not implemented locally.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/status-issuance-badge/reference.png`

### Badge Dot

Tiny colored dot with no text that signals presence or unread state, such as an online indicator or a new-activity mark on a tab.

Level: atom · Part of: AvatarWithStatus

Use when:
- Unread indicator on a TabBar item or notification bell
- Presence dot (this is the dot AvatarWithStatus reuses)
- "Has updates" mark on a list row where the count does not matter

Don't use when:
- Showing how many items are unread: use Badge Count
- Any status that needs words (Approved, Funded): use StatusPill or IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor)
- Presence on a user avatar: use AvatarWithStatus, which already composes the dot

Accessibility: Decorative to screen readers on its own; the parent must announce the state in text, for example "new notifications".

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tone | `tone` | variant | neutral, info, success, warning, error, brand | neutral |
| Size | `size` | variant | md, sm | md |

### Badge Count

Small numeric counter pill (3, 12, 99+) anchored to an icon or tab to show how many items need attention. Direction flips its anchor corner.

Level: atom · Part of: TabBar

Use when:
- Unread notification count on the bell or a TabBar item
- Number of pending KYC tasks or documents on a menu entry
- Count of new deal updates on a tab

Don't use when:
- Presence or unread without a number: use Badge Dot
- A text status label: use StatusPill
- A KPI number such as total invested: use Stat

Accessibility: Pair with an accessible label ("3 unread notifications"); cap at 99+ and keep Western digits.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

### IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor)

Locked-copy lifecycle badge that shows investors where a deal (issuance) sits: Reserved, Raising/Confirmed, Fully Funded, Active, Matured, Repayment Due, Late, Defaulted, Completed and so on. Color and Arabic/English copy come from the Issuance Status Copy spec and use raw per-phase palettes on purpose.

Level: atom · Contains: illustrations · Part of: CardDeal, Issuance Row, NewsCard / Poster Actions

Use when:
- Deal status on a CardDeal, portfolio card or investment history row seen by investors
- Status in an Issuance Row or NewsCard / Poster Actions
- Status label in push-notification previews or a deal header for investors

Don't use when:
- A developer-portal surface: use IssuanceStatusBadge (Developer)
- Admin or Monitoring dashboards: use IssuanceStatusBadge (Internal)
- Generic attributes outside the lifecycle (Verified, Premium, Expired): use StatusPill
- Sector or category labels: use Tag
- Deal tier or marketing ribbon (Premium, Basic, Closed tab): use dealTags
- Showing Reimbursed or PendingDrawdown to investors: never; the resolver maps them to Completed and Fully Funded

Accessibility: Status is carried by the label text (Arabic in RTL), never color alone; do not detach or recolor instances.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Status | `status` | variant | Reserved, Confirmed, Funded, Active, Matured, Late, Defaulted, Funding Failed, Fully Funded, Completed, Partially Repaid, Private Reservation, Repayment Due, Written Off, Cancelled | Reserved |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | LTR, RTL | LTR |

### IssuanceStatusBadge (Developer)

Lifecycle badge set for the developer portal, covering the 19 statuses developers see, including operational ones investors never see (ListingPreparation, PendingLaunch, PendingDrawdown "Transfer in progress", RepaymentMonitoring, Reimbursed "Investors paid").

Level: atom

Use when:
- Issuance list and detail screens in the developer portal
- Developer-facing notifications about funding, drawdown and repayment
- Showing a developer that Reimbursed means Safqah paid investors and their debt is not cleared

Don't use when:
- Any investor-facing surface: use IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor)
- Admin-only states (OnHold, Dispute, Rejected): use IssuanceStatusBadge (Internal)
- Non-lifecycle attributes: use StatusPill

Accessibility: Same as the investor set: label text carries the meaning; pick audience from the signed-in user, not from the data record.

### IssuanceStatusBadge (Internal)

Admin-only lifecycle badge for six internal states (ReadyForListing, PendingApproval, Rejected, ReservationsAllocated, OnHold, Dispute), English only and never user-facing.

Level: atom · Part of: Table / Cell

Use when:
- Monitoring team dashboards and back-office issuance tables
- Audit logs and ops tooling that track pre-listing review
- Back-office Table / Cell status columns

Don't use when:
- Investor screens: use IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor)
- Developer portal: use IssuanceStatusBadge (Developer)
- Generic back-office states unrelated to issuance (user verified, ticket open): use StatusPill

Accessibility: Label text is the semantic; ensure contrast on back-office table backgrounds.

Small isometric Isocon glyph set for deal lifecycle phases (Scheduled, Raising, Preparing, Active, Matured, Repayment due, In recovery, Defaulted), each with Right or Left alignment for RTL/LTR. It supplies the leading glyph inside IssuanceStatusBadge pills.

Level: atom · Part of: IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor), IssuanceStatusBadge (Developer)

Use when:
- Leading glyph inside an IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor) or (Developer) variant

Don't use when:
- Large empty-state or onboarding artwork: use Illustrations (the full Isocon set on the EmptyState page)

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Badge has two purposes in Safqah. The first is generic: indicate the existence of something (a notification, an unread message, a count). The second is domain-specific: communicate where an issuance sits in its 25-status lifecycle. The two purposes are deliberately separated into a primitive layer (Badge Dot, Badge Count) and a domain-application layer (IssuanceStatusBadge × 3 audiences) so the primitive stays reusable and the lifecycle badges stay tightly coupled to the canonical copy spec.

> **Warning:** IssuanceStatusBadge copy is derived from the "Issuance Status Copy - Safqah Capital" markdown spec. If a status label needs to change, change the markdown spec first and propagate downstream. Hand-editing the badge in Figma without updating the spec creates a silent divergence between the design system, the i18n keys, and the product copy.

### Family at a glance

### Visibility matrix - all 25 statuses

The markdown spec is explicit about which statuses are visible to each audience. This is the canonical reference: if a status is "Hidden" for an audience, it has no badge variant in that set. Where a cell shows a badge, that audience sees that exact badge in user-facing UI. Where it shows text, that audience either doesn't see a badge or sees a different status's badge via aliasing.

### Legend

- Visible - a badge variant exists in that audience's set and renders in user-facing UI.
- Participants - visible only to investors who pre-booked or invested (not to discovery surfaces or general lists).
- Whitelisted - visible only to specific investors who received a private reservation invitation from Safqah.
- Hidden - the status has no UI surface at all for that audience.
- Merged with Funded - PendingDrawdown reuses Funded's investor copy and badge; no separate variant exists.
- Reuses Repaid - Reimbursed reuses Repaid's investor copy and badge for investors. The developer sees the distinct "Investors paid" copy. This audience-asymmetry is the most operationally sensitive distinction in the entire spec.

### Atomic architecture - two layers, five sets

The badge family splits into two layers. Layer 1 is reusable primitives. Layer 2 is domain-specific applications tied to a copy spec.

Layer 1 · Badge Dot · 12 variants

Smallest possible status indicator. 6 tones × 2 sizes (sm/md). No text, no count, no shape variation - just a colored dot. Use for online/offline indicators on avatars, "has unread" indicators on tabs, or any "this thing has state X" pattern where the state itself doesn't need a number.

Layer 1 · Badge Count · 36 variants

6 tones × 3 sizes × 2 directions. Numeric overflow indicator - "3", "12", "99+". For notification counts, cart items, comment counts. Direction matters because numbers in Arabic locales sit visually on the same side but the badge anchor flips (LTR places counter top-right, RTL top-left).

Layer 2 · IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor) · 28 variants

14 statuses × 2 directions. Investor-facing surfaces: deal cards, portfolio cards, history records, push notifications, progress bar labels. Each status has its own hex palette tied to the lifecycle phase (pre-launch beige/violet → open blue/green → active mint → repayment amber/orange → terminal green/red/sepia). PendingDrawdown is intentionally omitted - for investors it merges into Funded per the copy spec.

Layer 2 · IssuanceStatusBadge (Developer) · 38 variants

19 statuses × 2 directions. Developer-portal-facing. Larger surface than investor because developers see pre-launch and operational states that investors never see (ListingPreparation, PendingLaunch, BookBuilding, PendingDrawdown, RepaymentMonitoring, Reimbursed). Reimbursed copy in particular ("Investors paid") is operationally critical - prevents the misconception that investor reimbursement clears the developer's debt.

Layer 2 · IssuanceStatusBadge (Internal) · 6 variants

6 admin-only statuses, single direction (admin English only). Never user-facing. Used in Monitoring team dashboards, ops tools, and audit logs to surface internal states (ReadyForListing, PendingApproval, Rejected, ReservationsAllocated, OnHold, Dispute) that don't exist for investors or developers.

### Locked invariants - two audience-asymmetries

Two statuses have intentionally different behavior between investor and developer audiences. These are not bugs or accidents - they are baked into the markdown copy spec because the underlying operational reality is asymmetric. Tooling, runtime, and design must all enforce these invariants.

Invariant 1 · Reimbursed === Repaid (for investors)

When Safqah pays investors out of its own balance sheet on a defaulted issuance, the investor sees this as "Completed / مكتمل" - same badge as Repaid. From the investor's perspective, the money is back; the distinction between "developer paid us" and "Safqah paid us" is meaningless to them and would create alarm if surfaced. The developer, however, sees "Investors paid / المستثمرون استلموا" - making it operationally clear that their debt has NOT been cleared.

Investor sees →

(reuses Repaid badge - no separate variant)

Developer sees →

> **Warning:** Enforcement layer 1 (Figma): no Reimbursed variant exists in the Investor set. If you try to create one, this constraint must be re-discussed first. Enforcement layer 2 (i18n): the i18n key `issuance.status.Reimbursed.investor` is intentionally absent - the resolver falls through to `issuance.status.Repaid.investor`. Enforcement layer 3 (CI): a snapshot test asserts that the runtime Reimbursed display === Repaid display for any locale + audience=investor combination.

Invariant 2 · PendingDrawdown === Funded (for investors)

The transfer-being-prepared operational phase is invisible to investors. They see the issuance as "Fully funded / اكتمل التمويل" until the moment the developer's account is credited and the status moves to Active. The developer has a distinct "Transfer in progress / التحويل قيد التنفيذ" badge so they know to expect the deposit and the confirmation message.

Investor sees →

(reuses Funded badge - no separate variant)

Developer sees →

> **Warning:** Enforcement: same 3-layer pattern as Invariant 1. The investor i18n key `issuance.status.PendingDrawdown.investor` falls through to `Funded.investor`; the runtime status resolver maps PendingDrawdown→Funded for investor contexts; CI snapshot test asserts equality.

### Phase taxonomy - 7 lifecycle phases

The 25 statuses group into 7 phases. Each phase has a distinct visual character in the badge palette so users develop pattern-recognition for "where in the lifecycle is this issuance" without having to read individual labels.

Pre-launch

Internal preparation phase. Most statuses (4 of 5) are admin-only; only ListingPreparation and PendingLaunch surface to the developer. No investor visibility. Palette: warm beige and violet - signals "not yet open."

Developer badges →

Open for investment

The window when investors can commit capital. Scheduled (pre-launch reservation) and Raising (public window) are the two visible states for both audiences; BookBuilding is whitelisted-only. Palette: blue and green - "active and inviting."

Investor badges →

Developer badges →

Funded → drawdown

Target reached, transfer being prepared, then capital deployed. Active is the longest-lived state in the entire lifecycle (often 12-36 months). Palette: mint and green - "achieved, working."

Investor badges →

Developer badges →

Repayment journey

The path from maturity through possible escalation. RepaymentMonitoring is a 90-day developer-only warning; Matured is the 15-day grace window; RepaymentDue → Late → Defaulted is the escalation path if repayment doesn't arrive. Palette: violet (matured), amber (overdue), orange (recovery), red (default) - "increasing concern."

Investor badges →

Developer badges →

Terminal - successful

Issuance closed with capital returning to investors. Repaid is the happy ending; Reimbursed has audience-asymmetric copy (see Locked Invariants); PartiallyRepaid is the middle outcome. Palette: deep green - "completed."

Investor badges →

Developer badges →

Terminal - unsuccessful

Issuance closed without full recovery. WrittenOff (recovery exhausted), Cancelled (pulled before completion), FundingFailed (target not reached) all live here. Palette: sepia, neutral, deep red - "not what we hoped, but final."

Investor badges →

Developer badges →

Exception

OnHold (reversible pause) and Dispute (contested) - both admin-only, never user-facing. Handled at the system level. No badge appears to investors or developers; the Monitoring team works through these in operations tooling.

No user-facing badges in this phase - admin tooling only.

### Direction - LTR + RTL with font fallback

Every IssuanceStatusBadge variant exists in both LTR (English, IBM Plex Sans Medium) and RTL (Arabic, Noto Sans Arabic Medium) directions. The font choice for Arabic is intentional - IBM Plex Sans does not reliably render all Arabic glyphs in this Figma file, and substituting Noto Sans Arabic produces clean, readable Arabic at the small badge size.

LTR (IBM Plex Sans Medium) →

RTL (Noto Sans Arabic Medium) →

> **Warning:** Font choice note: IBM Plex Sans Arabic is NOT installed in this Figma file (verified via figma.listAvailableFontsAsync). The IBM Plex Sans Medium style renders some Arabic strings correctly but fails on others (notably multi-character ligatures like "مكتمل"). Noto Sans Arabic Medium is the chosen substitute - visually consistent with IBM Plex Sans at small sizes and produces clean Arabic glyphs. Mixed-font-per-direction is intentional. If IBM Plex Sans Arabic is ever installed, regenerate all RTL variants to use the matched font for visual consistency.

### Color tokens - per-status palettes

IssuanceStatusBadge uses raw hex values, NOT semantic tokens. This is an intentional locked invariant: the 25-status palette is the lifecycle-phase color encoding (warm beige for pre-launch, amber for overdue, deep red for default, etc) and decoupling it from semantic tokens prevents accidental theme-level changes from breaking the lifecycle reading. Every other component in the system uses semantic tokens; IssuanceStatusBadge is the exception. Maintenance cost is documented in the Notes section.

> **Info:** These hex values are the source of truth. If you need to change a status palette, update both this section AND the Figma component instance fills - the runtime Dart code reads from this palette table. To prevent drift, a build step generates this Dart code from the same data structure used to build the Figma component sets.

### Code examples - Flutter

Reference implementations. Real production code lives in `lib/design_system/badge/`. These examples illustrate the 3-layer enforcement of the audience-asymmetry invariants.

### Single badge usage

```dart
// Render a status badge - audience is resolved at render time from session context.
// The runtime maps PendingDrawdown→Funded and Reimbursed→Repaid for investor audiences.
IssuanceStatusBadge(
  status: issuance.status,
  audience: BadgeAudience.investor,  // or .developer, .internal
)

// Internally this resolves to:
// 1. Look up effective status (apply invariant mapping for audience)
// 2. Look up palette from {audience}_palette.dart
// 3. Look up label from i18n: issuance.status.{effectiveStatus}.{audience}.label
// 4. Look up direction from current locale (LTR/RTL)
// 5. Render pill with palette + label + correct font for direction
```

### Status resolver (invariant enforcement)

```dart
// File: lib/design_system/badge/status_resolver.dart
class BadgeStatusResolver {
  /// Apply audience-specific invariant mappings.
  /// This is the SINGLE point where invariants are enforced.
  static IssuanceStatus resolveForAudience(
    IssuanceStatus status,
    BadgeAudience audience,
  ) {
    if (audience == BadgeAudience.investor) {
      // Invariant 1: Reimbursed === Repaid for investors
      if (status == IssuanceStatus.reimbursed) return IssuanceStatus.repaid;
      // Invariant 2: PendingDrawdown === Funded for investors
      if (status == IssuanceStatus.pendingDrawdown) return IssuanceStatus.funded;
    }
    return status;
  }
}
```

### CI snapshot test (regression guard)

```dart
// File: test/design_system/badge/invariant_test.dart
void main() {
  group('IssuanceStatusBadge audience-asymmetry invariants', () {
    test('Invariant 1: Reimbursed renders identically to Repaid for investors', () {
      for (final locale in [Locale('en'), Locale('ar')]) {
        final reimbursed = renderBadge(
          status: IssuanceStatus.reimbursed,
          audience: BadgeAudience.investor,
          locale: locale,
        );
        final repaid = renderBadge(
          status: IssuanceStatus.repaid,
          audience: BadgeAudience.investor,
          locale: locale,
        );
        expect(reimbursed.label, equals(repaid.label));
        expect(reimbursed.colors, equals(repaid.colors));
      }
    });

    test('Invariant 2: PendingDrawdown renders identically to Funded for investors', () {
      for (final locale in [Locale('en'), Locale('ar')]) {
        final pending = renderBadge(
          status: IssuanceStatus.pendingDrawdown,
          audience: BadgeAudience.investor,
          locale: locale,
        );
        final funded = renderBadge(
          status: IssuanceStatus.funded,
          audience: BadgeAudience.investor,
          locale: locale,
        );
        expect(pending.label, equals(funded.label));
        expect(pending.colors, equals(funded.colors));
      }
    });

    test('Reimbursed for developer renders distinct copy', () {
      final devReimbursed = renderBadge(
        status: IssuanceStatus.reimbursed,
        audience: BadgeAudience.developer,
        locale: Locale('en'),
      );
      expect(devReimbursed.label, equals('Investors paid'));
    });
  });
}
```

### Do and Don't

Four pairs of operational guidance. Each addresses a specific risk that arose during the markdown spec review.

### Investor never sees "Reimbursed"

- **Do** · Scenario name: For investor surfaces, always use IssuanceStatusBadge(status: ..., audience: BadgeAudience.investor) - the runtime maps Reimbursed→Repaid automatically. The investor sees "Completed / مكتمل".
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Never inject a Reimbursed badge directly into investor-facing UI. Doing so leaks the operational distinction ("Safqah paid us" vs "developer paid us") which is meaningless to investors and would create alarm.

### Investor never sees "PendingDrawdown"

- **Do** · Scenario name: For investor surfaces, the runtime maps PendingDrawdown→Funded. Investor sees "Fully funded / اكتمل التمويل" while the developer-side transfer is being prepared.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Never show "Transfer in progress / التحويل قيد التنفيذ" to an investor. This is developer-only operational state.

### Audience matches user, not data

- **Do** · Scenario name: Choose audience from the session user, not from the database record. The same Issuance row can render different badges in different surfaces simultaneously.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Do not derive audience from the Issuance entity itself. The Issuance does not have an "audience" - the surface does.

### Internal set is not user-facing

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use IssuanceStatusBadge(audience: BadgeAudience.internal) only in admin tooling - Monitoring team dashboards, audit logs, ops surfaces. The 6 internal statuses (ReadyForListing, PendingApproval, Rejected, etc) have no investor/developer counterparts.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Do not expose internal badges to investors or developers. If you find yourself needing one of these statuses in a user-facing surface, that is a spec-level decision and the markdown source of truth needs to be updated first.

### Notes from the maintainer

Known maintenance costs, design decisions that deserve revisiting, and policies that should not be quietly changed.

> **Warning:** Maintenance cost: raw hex palette. IssuanceStatusBadge is the only component in Syntropy that uses raw hex instead of semantic tokens. This is intentional but expensive: the 14+19+6 = 39 status palette entries × bg/fg/border = 117 hex values, each defined in 3 places (Figma component variant, Dart palette table, this doc page). A drift detector should run in CI to verify the three sources agree.

> **Warning:** Three-layer invariant enforcement is non-negotiable. The Reimbursed→Repaid and PendingDrawdown→Funded mappings are enforced in (1) Figma - no Investor variant exists, (2) i18n - key falls through to the merged status, (3) CI - snapshot tests assert runtime equality. If any future contributor adds a Reimbursed Investor variant, they must also delete the i18n alias and disable the CI test. That should be impossible without going through this doc page first.

> **Info:** Internal set is admin-only. The 6 internal statuses (ReadyForListing, PendingApproval, Rejected, ReservationsAllocated, OnHold, Dispute) exist for Monitoring team dashboards and audit logs. They have no investor/developer counterparts. If a future product requirement needs to show one of these to investors or developers, that is a markdown spec change first, not a Figma change.

> **Info:** Arabic font fallback is a known compromise. Noto Sans Arabic is used instead of IBM Plex Sans Arabic because the latter is not installed in this Figma file. If IBM Plex Sans Arabic is ever added, regenerate all RTL variants with the matched font for visual consistency.

> **Info:** No dark mode yet. IssuanceStatusBadge has Light mode palettes only. Dark mode is a documented gap. When defined, dark palettes will need WCAG re-verification against dark backgrounds.

> **Tip:** Phase color logic is the source of legibility. Pre-launch (warm beige/violet) → Open (blue/green) → Active (mint/green) → Repayment (amber/orange/red) → Terminal-successful (deep green) → Terminal-unsuccessful (sepia/neutral/deep red). Users develop pattern-recognition for the lifecycle without reading labels. Any new status or palette change must preserve this gradient.

> **Info:** BookBuilding is whitelisted-only on the investor side. The badge variant exists in the Investor set because whitelisted investors do see it (in push notifications, acceptance screen) - but it should never appear in discovery surfaces (deal lists, search results, public portfolio sharing). Surface gating is a runtime concern, not a badge concern.

> **Tip:** Future: add icons to IssuanceStatusBadge. Current variants are text-only because the small badge size (~32px tall) makes icons too cramped. A future v2.1 of the badge may add an Icon=hidden|leading boolean prop and a 24-icon set mapped 1:1 to the statuses. The Streamline icon pack used in 02. Actions has candidates.

> **Info:** i18n keys are stored alongside the labels in this doc page section "Code examples". The Notion markdown spec is the ultimate source of truth - if labels are edited there, propagate to (1) Figma component instance text, (2) Flutter i18n bundle, (3) this doc page.

> **Warning:** Do not detach IssuanceStatusBadge instances. Detached instances cannot be tracked by the design system audit script and create silent drift. If you need a one-off badge style, request a new variant or add it to the spec.
